source_text: Quod forsitan dicam, Scripturarum, non syllogismorum debere testimonio comprobari, filios de corporum commixtione nascentes, reputari divino operi Ut exprimeret fidem operum Propheta, prope periculum pudoris accessit, quia dixit: Erunt duo in carne una
pass_a_gloss: That/which perhaps dicam, of-the-Scriptures, not syllogismorum to-owe testimonio comprobari, sons about/from of-bodies by-mixing nascentes, reputari divino operi so-that/as exprimeret faith operum prophet, near periculum modesty it-was-added, because he-said: Erunt two in in-flesh together.
pass_b_english: Perhaps [he will say] that we must establish from the testimony of Scripture, rather than from syllogisms, that children born from bodily union are to be counted as God’s work.
To state faithfully how these works take place, the prophet came close to risking modesty, because he said: “The two will be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24).

choices.why: Julian's sacred writings; keep Scripture, not 'Bible' as a later book-name.
Opening fides promissionis is the pledge of a promise, not the theological virtue.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
